doc.title: Bob Havens interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997

title: Branson theatre and feelings about the showmanship routine
summary: Playing in the Lawrence Welk Theatre in Branson, and his reluctance about the acrobatic grandstanding he does for audiences.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: Well it’s curious because last week, I was just reading about you and I turned on the television and I’ll be darned if there wasn’t a Lawrence Welk special on, it was hosted by — I can’t remember her name, the blonde woman who played the kind of rag-timey piano?
Yeah. So she was hosting the show and they were doing this show, little spots. And they featured you on a thing, you came out front.

I had just started playing in Branson, Missouri this last April — Lawrence Welk’s son, Larry Junior, four years ago built a theatre in Branson, and now there’s a Lawrence Welk Theatre, and he asked me to come in and do a season with the band. So I’ve been there since April and I’ll be there through December of this year.

Well you were doing — I can’t remember the name of the tune — but at the end of it you were doing a little grandstanding you know? And I was curious if this was a thing that they encouraged you to do?

Well basically I’m a very mild-mannered trombone player. And I sort of have a laid back — and that sort of thing is not my real personality. And that’s why I really don’t enjoy doing that sort of thing, but I do know that the audience likes to see it. So I have just sort of forced myself to keep doing it throughout my career. And so I guess you have to do the bad things along with the good you know sometimes. And I don’t really enjoy doing that sort of thing, it’s just sort of exhibitionism, jumping around and doing all those acrobatic things. It’s not my personality because I’m very quiet basically.
